subject: Unc
title: What does unc mean? The slang term Gen Z uses for "uncool"
answer: In current slang, "unc" means someone who is out of touch or uncool, often an older person who "just doesn't get it." It is a clipping of "uncle." Dictionary.com put unc on its 2026 Word of the Year shortlist and compared it to "OK Boomer."
body:
Unc comes from African American Vernacular English, where it was used affectionately or respectfully for an older man in the family or a mentor, according to Dictionary.com. In 2026, Gen Z and Gen Alpha began using it as a jab at anyone who seems corny or behind the times. Dictionary.com put it this way: "Think of it like the new 'OK Boomer,' signifying that Gen Z is now the driving force of culture."

The tone depends on who is talking. Among friends or family it can still be warm, a nickname for an uncle or an older friend. Aimed at a stranger, it usually means "you're old and out of touch." It is also written in all capitals, "UNC," which is not the same as the abbreviation for the University of North Carolina.

Unc made Dictionary.com's 2026 shortlist alongside affordability, data center and odyssey. The winner was maxxing.
in_the_news: Dictionary.com named unc to its 2026 Word of the Year shortlist, announced Oct. 25, 2026.

faq.q: What does unc mean in slang?
faq.a: Someone out of touch or uncool, usually older. It is short for "uncle."

faq.q: Is calling someone unc an insult?
faq.a: It can be. Gen Z often uses it as a jab, but it can also be an affectionate nickname for an uncle or an older friend.
From African American Vernacular English, where it was a respectful or affectionate term for older male relatives and mentors.

faq.q: Is unc the new OK Boomer?
faq.a: Dictionary.com makes that comparison, saying unc signals "that Gen Z is now the driving force of culture."

faq.q: Was unc the 2026 Word of the Year?
faq.a: No. It was on Dictionary.com's shortlist; the winner was maxxing.
